olivia: We need a single canonical loadtest protocol for kernel/batching/KV cache comparisons. Can we settle TTFT/TPOT defs + what to measure? Looking to avoid apples-to-apples drift. Who's in for a short checklist? :clipboard:

sam: Proposed defs: TTFT = time from request arrival to first token emitted (median/p95/p99). TPOT = tokens per second observed per GPU across steady-state period (exclude first token). Goodput = tokens/sec that actually caused model computation (exclude pure cache hits where applicable) vs QPS = requests/sec. We should report both. Thoughts?

miguel: Agree. Need to emphasize KV-cache warmup: prefix cache makes first N requests cheaper. For replay harness we should tag requests with `cache_hit=true` and compute metrics with/without cold-starts. Synthetic traffic often misses temporal locality.

ci-bot: Perf run 2024-04-18 14:02: logs uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/runs/1713456789
Summary: p95 TTFT: 72ms (+12% from baseline), TPOT steady: 48k tok/s, KV-cache hit-rate: 37%.

noah: If helpful, minimal load config I use:
```
--clients 200
--arrival dist=poisson,lam=40
--prompt-mix small_instruct:0.6,chat_short:0.4
--duration 20m
--measure warmup=120s,steady=5m
```
Use `--measure warmup=...` to separate first-token effects.

anya: Sanity checklist for every benchmark:
- include raw traces
- report med/p95/p99 TTFT
- TPOT vs GPU utilization
- KV-cache decomposition (cold/partial/hit)
- synthetic vs replay comparison table
- attach topdown flame/profile for p95 outliers
Also add a gating rule: >10% p95 regression needs rollback.

sam: For regression thresholds: prefer relative + absolute. Eg p95 TTFT increase >10% and >20ms -> fail. TPOT drop >8% and >200 tok/s -> fail. Goodput vs QPS: compute `goodput_ratio = goodput / (qps * avg_tokens_per_request)` and flag if deviates >7%.

miguel: Kernel sweep plan: pick 3 kernels (fast-atten, fused-attn, alt-kernel). Run 3 seeds per kernel, each with 5m steady window. Collect per-layer op times, memory allocs. Use profiling hooks: `--profile layers,allocs,cupti` and export to perf-bench.

olivia: Nice. Can someone (sam?) codify into a runner script and add to perf harness? Also add a `kvcache-warmup` toggle to simulate user sessions. I'll use results in the next ops review.

sam: @olivia I'll add the runner this afternoon. Will include the gating thresholds and a docs checklist. I'll post PR link here when ready. :+1:

ci-bot: Created perf-job #1723 (draft). Running kernel sweep is queued.

olivia: Thanks all. Action items: sam = runner + PR, miguel = profile config & sample outputs, noah = canonical load config, anya = add gating to CI policy. We'll reconvene after first sweep. :calendar:
